hints: For a pile size s, a move subtracts one of the allowed numbers.
A position is winning if some legal move reaches a losing position.
Compute winning/losing status from smaller pile sizes up to n.
analogy: A position is safe if you can move to a state where the next player has no winning move.
correctness: Every move decreases the pile, so all successor states are already classified; the winning definition directly yields this recurrence.
algorithm: Read n, the number of stones to classify, and the k allowed move sizes. Set win[0]=false. For s=1..n, set win[s]=true if some allowed move x<=s has win[s-x]==false; otherwise false. Print W/L for sizes 1..n as the statement requests.
complexity: O(nk) time and O(n) space, where k is the number of allowed move sizes.
example: With allowed moves {1,3}, pile size 2 is losing: the only legal move removes 1 and leaves size 1, which is winning for the next player.
